claim: Guy's Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 3rd ed. (2004), Section D (Diophantine Equations, pp.209-310) is subdivided into exactly 29 titled subsections D1-D29, none of which is titled anything resembling 'pairs of triples with equal sum and equal sum of reciprocals'.
stance_target: existence of Section 5's problem as a titled subsection in Guy's UPINT
quoted_support: D. Diophantine Equations 209 ... D11. Egyptian fractions. 252 D12. Markoff numbers. 263 D13. The equation x^x y^y = z^z. 265 ... D16. Triples with the same sum and same product. 271 ... D28. A reciprocal diophantine equation. 309 D29. Diophantine m-tuples. 310

claim: Section D11 'Egyptian fractions' occupies pp.252-262 (ending where D12 begins at p.263) in the 3rd edition, consistent with the 2nd-edition page range pp.158-166 cited independently by MathWorld.
stance_target: exact location of the Egyptian-fractions section across editions
quoted_support: D11. Egyptian fractions. 252 D12. Markoff numbers. 263

claim: Section D16 'Triples with the same sum and same product' (p.271) is the structurally closest subsection in Guy's UPINT to a pairs-of-triples numeric coincidence, but its second matched invariant is PRODUCT, not sum of reciprocals, making it a different problem from Section 5's target.
stance_target: identity of D16 with Section 5's equal-sum-equal-reciprocal-sum problem
quoted_support: D16. Triples with the same sum and same product. 271

claim: Section D28 'A reciprocal diophantine equation' (p.309) is the only subsection title in Guy's UPINT containing the word 'reciprocal', but it concerns a single 4-variable Mordell-type equation, not a pairs-of-triples coincidence.
stance_target: identity of D28 with Section 5's problem

claim: The 3rd edition (2004) added new problems on symmetric and asymmetric primes, sums of higher powers, Diophantine m-tuples, and Conway's RATS and palindromes relative to the 2nd edition, plus OEIS cross-references at the end of many sections.
stance_target: scope of revisions in the 3rd edition
quoted_support: For this new edition, the author has included new problems on symmetric and asymmetric primes, sums of higher powers, Diophantine m-tuples, and Conway's RATS and palindromes.
